question: Which of the following is an example of an indirect tax?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Tax:** An indirect tax is a tax imposed on goods and services rather than on income or profits. Consumers pay this tax indirectly as part of the purchase price of goods or services.
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST):** GST is a comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services across India. It is a multi-stage, destination-based tax system aimed at eliminating cascading taxes.
 
• GST is categorized as an indirect tax because it is collected by businesses from consumers at the point of sale and remitted to the government. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• Income Tax (Option 1): It is a direct tax levied on an individual's or entity's income by the government. *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
• Corporate Tax (Option 2): This is a direct tax imposed on the net income or profit of companies. *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
• Wealth Tax (Option 4): This is a direct tax levied on the net wealth of an individual, entity, or Hindu Undivided Family (HUF). *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Indirect Taxes:**

 
 
• Indirect taxes are levied on the consumption of goods and services and are ultimately paid by the end consumer.
 
• The seller or service provider collects the tax from consumers and remits it to the government.
 
• Examples of indirect taxes include **GST, customs duty, excise duty, and value-added tax (VAT).**
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of GST:**
 
 
• GST was introduced in **India on 1st July 2017** under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• It is classified into **Central GST (CGST)** and **State GST (SGST)** for intra-state transactions and **Integrated GST (IGST)** for inter-state transactions.
 
• GST replaced multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, VAT, and customs duty, streamlining the taxation system in India.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of GST:**
 
 
• Eliminates cascading taxes and reduces the overall tax burden on consumers.
 
• Promotes ease of doing business by providing a unified taxation system.
 
• Encourages transparency in tax collection and compliance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Understanding Direct Taxes vs. Indirect Taxes:**

 
 
• **Direct Taxes:** Levied directly on an individual's or entity's income, wealth, or profit. Examples include **income tax, corporate tax, and wealth tax.**
 
• **Indirect Taxes:** Applied to goods and services, and the burden is passed on to the end consumer. Examples include **GST, customs duty, and excise duty.**
 
 
 
• **Global Adoption of GST:**
 
 
• Over **160 countries** globally have implemented GST or similar value-added taxes, including **Canada, Australia, and European Union nations.**
 
• It is recognized as an efficient taxation model to promote economic growth and reduce tax evasion.
